pageDescription: Who can open the back office, and what each of them may reach. Access is a set of permissions per account — there are no roles.
emptyFiltered: Clear the filters to see every account.
emptyFirst: The first superuser is created from the command line — see script/create-admin.ts.
deleteDescription: {email} loses access immediately and every session they have open ends. Disabling the account keeps the record and is reversible.
setPasswordFor: For {email}. Every session they have open is ended.
passwordMismatch: The two passwords do not match.
passwordSetToast: Password set. {email} was signed out everywhere.
sheetDescription: Back-office accounts only. Customers sign in through the storefront and share nothing with this list.
noPasswordNotice: This account has no password and cannot sign in. Use "Set password" on its row.
cannotDisableSelf: You cannot disable your own account
nameInvalid: Enter a name of at least 2 characters.
selfAccessLocked: You cannot change your own access. Ask another administrator.
assignNeeded: You can edit this profile, but not what it reaches — that needs {permission}.
superuserInfo: A superuser passes every check, including permissions added to the panel later — which is why granting the whole list by hand is not the same thing. There must always be at least one, or nobody can grant access again.
superuserOn: Holds everything, now and in future. The selection below is kept but not consulted.
superuserOff: Off — access is exactly the permissions selected below.
superuserOnlySuper: Only a superuser can hand this out.
setsInfo: A set is a shortcut, not a role: clicking it copies its permissions into the selection and is then forgotten. Nothing at runtime resolves a set, so editing one later never changes what an existing account can reach.
lockedNotice.one: {count} permission is dimmed: you cannot grant access you do not hold yourself.
lockedNotice.other: {count} permissions are dimmed: you cannot grant access you do not hold yourself.
